questions.explain: The three-tier model: Tier 1 autonomous (online index WITH (ONLINE=ON), stats updates, KILL of long-running sessions), Tier 2 approval-required (blocking rebuild, KILL, config changes — 15-minute Slack approval window, timeout = rejected + escalate), Tier 3 human-only (DROP TABLE/index, ALTER PRIMARY KEY, promote standby, DROP DATABASE).
options: Tier 1 autonomous (bounded, reversible actions like an ONLINE index build or stats update); Tier 2 propose-and-await-approval (blocking rebuilds, KILL, config changes with a 15-minute window; timeout = rejected and escalated); Tier 3 human-only (DROP TABLE/index, ALTER PRIMARY KEY, promote standby, DROP DATABASE) — never executed
Tier 1 actions need CEO approval, Tier 2 need DBA approval, Tier 3 needs vendor support
Tiers are decided by the LLM in its reasoning trace; dispatch_tool only logs the decision
Tier 1 executes during peak hours only, Tier 2 during maintenance windows, Tier 3 is for cloud resources

questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: this tiering is enforced in the dispatch_tool function, not in the agent's reasoning — LLMs can be persuaded; code cannot (easily).

In the LLM's model weights after fine-tuning on past approvals

questions.explain: The audit table is append-only: the agent's writer role is granted INSERT but explicitly DENYed UPDATE and DELETE, giving tamper evidence when explaining an autonomous action — plus every action is also pushed to a Redis audit list and given a hashed action_id.
